title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page): k is algebraically closed. X^n is smooth, connected and projective, and Y^{n-1} is a smooth hyperplane section. The notation is:
- A^i_r: codimension-i cycles modulo rational equivalence.
- A^i_a: modulo algebraic equivalence.
- A^i_τ: modulo τ-equivalence, i.e. some multiple is algebraically equivalent to 0.
- A_r(X)^τ: the subgroup of A_r that is τ-equivalent to 0 (the 'continuous' or algebraically-trivial part).
- Lower index (A^r_i, A^a_i, A^τ_i): dimension-i cycles, with the equivalence relation written as a superscript.
- 'exc. p': up to p-torsion phenomena in characteristic p.
- 'mod groupes finis': in the Serre class of finite groups.
The page continues a list of conjectural 'Lefschetz theorems for cycle groups', modelled on weak and hard Lefschetz in cohomology.

Top of page, end of item ② (Gysin push-forward A_i(Y) → A_i(X) of dimension-i cycles). For 2i = n-1 the claim is that A^τ_i(Y) → A^τ_i(X) (cycles modulo τ-equivalence) is surjective, except p. Cohomological model: Gysin H^{n-1}(Y) → H^{n+1}(X) is dual to the restriction H^{n-1}(X) → H^{n-1}(Y). That restriction is injective by weak Lefschetz, so the Gysin map is surjective. The statement is consistent with this, once A^τ_i is read as 'cycles mod τ' and not as 'the τ-subgroup'.

Item ③, hard Lefschetz for cycle groups. Here E is intersection with the hyperplane class (called L on the next page).
(i) For 2i ≤ n, E^{n-2i}: A^i_a(X) → A^{n-i}_a(X) is bijective mod finite groups. This was first written 'injectif exc. p' and corrected to 'bijectif mod groupes finis'. A crossed-out duplicate for A_τ is redundant, since A_τ = A_a modulo torsion.
(ii) For 2i-1 ≤ n, E^{n-2i+1}: A^i_r(X)^τ (with an unclear subscript 1) → A^{n-i+1}_r(X)^τ is bijective mod finite groups. Model: hard Lefschetz L^{n-2i+1}: H^{2i-1} → H^{2n-2i+1}. The τ-part of codimension-i Chow is the 'intermediate abelian variety' attached to H^{2i-1}.

Consequence (⇒), for E^p: A^i_r(X) → A^{i+p}_r(X):
(a) injective mod finite groups if p ≤ n-2i;
(b) surjective mod finite groups if p ≥ n-2i+1.
The deduction uses the two-step dévissage 0 → A_r^τ → A_r → A_τ (≈ A_a mod finite) → 0. On the A_a graded piece, L^{n-2i} bijective gives injectivity of L^p for p ≤ n-2i. For j = i+p ≥ n-i+1, factor the bijection L^{2j-n} through A^i to get surjectivity. The τ-piece is handled the same way with exponent n-2i+1, and the five lemma (mod finite groups) assembles the two pieces.

Purpose: a full conjectural 'Lefschetz package' (weak and hard) for Chow groups and for cycles mod algebraic equivalence. It is a cycle-level strengthening of the standard conjectures of Lefschetz type. The next page uses it to predict Chow groups of the affine complement X−Y and of the punctured affine cone. There the 'primitive parts' Ker L^{n-2i} on A_a, and Ker L^{n-2i+1} on the intermediate-abelian-variety part, appear.
errors: ③(i), hard Lefschetz modulo algebraic equivalence 'mod groupes finis', is false over C. Take n=3, i=1, X a general quintic threefold. NS(X)=Z, but A^2_a(X) contains the Griffiths group, which is non-torsion (Griffiths 1969) and even of infinite rank (Clemens 1983). So E: A^1_a → A^2_a is not surjective mod finite groups. The statement is only plausible over fields like F̄_p, where algebraic and numerical equivalence are expected to agree mod torsion.

③(ii) on the full τ-part of Chow groups is false over C. Take n=2, i=1: E: Pic^τ(X) → CH_0(X)^τ cannot be surjective mod finite groups when p_g > 0 (Mumford 1969). It survives only if the subscript '1' means the abelian-variety quotient (algebraic representative / Abel–Jacobi image). Even then the deduction (b) needs A_r^τ = A_r^τ_1 mod finite groups, which is false.

Conclusion (b), surjectivity of E^p on Chow groups mod finite groups for p ≥ n-2i+1, is false over C. Mumford's example (surface, i=1, p=1, Pic → CH_0) refutes it. A Bloch–Beilinson-style filtration analysis shows surjectivity on Gr^ν_F needs p ≥ n-2i+ν, so (b) only accounts for ν ≤ 1. Conclusion (a) is consistent with Bloch–Beilinson with Q-coefficients.
The deduction ⇒ silently assumes a two-step filtration (A_a part plus one 'abelian' part) on Chow groups up to finite groups. This is exactly what Mumford's theorem rules out over large fields.

ideas.what: Weak-Lefschetz (Gysin) surjectivity for dimension-(n-1)/2 cycles mod τ-equivalence from a hyperplane section to X
ideas.modern_name: Lefschetz hyperplane theorem for cycle groups / Chow groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hartshorne (1975, 'Equivalence relations on algebraic cycles and subvarieties of small codimension'); later as consequences of Bloch–Beilinson–Murre
ideas.where_published: Not in the 1969 'Standard conjectures' paper, which treats only cohomological/numerical versions; the Picard case is in SGA 2

ideas.what: Hard Lefschetz L^{n-2i}: A^i_a → A^{n-i}_a bijective mod finite groups (cycles mod algebraic equivalence)
ideas.modern_name: Hard Lefschetz for cycles modulo algebraic equivalence (strengthening of standard conjecture B)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck's standard conjecture B (numerical version); the algebraic-equivalence version is refuted over C by Griffiths/Clemens
ideas.where_published: Only the homological/numerical form: Grothendieck, 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (1969)

ideas.what: Hard Lefschetz L^{n-2i+1} between τ-parts (intermediate abelian varieties) of codimension i and n-i+1, an isogeny-type statement
ideas.modern_name: Lefschetz conjecture for algebraic representatives / Lieberman's algebraic intermediate Jacobians
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lieberman (1972, intermediate Jacobians); Murre (algebraic representatives); Vial and Achter–Casalaina-Martin–Vial (recent)

ideas.what: Derived injectivity/surjectivity ranges for E^p on Chow groups via the two-step dévissage A_r^τ ⊂ A_r → A_τ
ideas.modern_name: Lefschetz-type statements for Chow groups (Bloch–Beilinson / Murre consequences)

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulated, in unpublished notes, integral ('mod finite groups', 'except p') hard-Lefschetz conjectures for cycles modulo algebraic equivalence and for the algebraically-trivial part of Chow groups, over an arbitrary algebraically closed field. These naive conjectures were later refuted over C by Griffiths (1969) and Mumford (1969). They document that Grothendieck initially expected Chow groups to have a two-step, cohomology-like structure. That expectation was abandoned and replaced by the infinite-filtration picture of Bloch–Beilinson.
missed.quote: A^i_a(X) --E^{n-2i}--> A^{n-i}_a(X) (2i≤n) ... bijectif mod groupes finis ... ⟹ A^i_r(X) --E^p--> A^{i+p}_r(X) ... b) surjectif mod groupes finis si p ≥ n-2i+1
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historically, it shows that the cycle-level Lefschetz conjectures were present in Grothendieck's program before Griffiths and Mumford. Mathematically, the statements remain meaningful over F̄_p and over number fields (mod torsion). There they align with the Tate, Beilinson and standard conjectures. The abelian-variety version is an active topic (algebraic representatives).

deep.surprise_reason: An unpublished, explicit Lefschetz package for cycles mod algebraic and rational equivalence, with careful 'exc. p' and 'mod finite groups' caveats. It is historically interesting but largely false over C (Griffiths, Mumford). Its true parts are standard consequences of the standard and Bloch–Beilinson conjectures, so it is not new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: The arrows in ③ are labelled E^{n-2i}, E^{n-2i+1}, E^p (E = hyperplane-class operator, later L), and should not be read otherwise.
In the second line of ③ the source is written A^i_r(X)^τ with a small mark '1' under τ; the reading 'τ_1' is uncertain and may be a stray subscript.
In the top line, A^τ_i(Y), A^τ_i(X) has the equivalence relation as a superscript (dimension-i cycles mod τ-equivalence), matching the A^r_i, A^a_i notation of ②. It is not the τ-subgroup.
The struck-out first line under ③ reads 'injectif exc. p', with 'bijectif' written above it, followed by 'mod groupes finis'.
